responsibility: This module is GCC’s 32-bit Arm target backend, responsible for turning generic GCC IR into correct and efficient ARM/Thumb code across Arm architectures, ABIs, operating-system environments, and microarchitectures. Its core files define target hooks, option parsing, ABI and object-format policy, register/addressing rules, prologue/epilogue generation, asm emission, and overall instruction-selection strategy; the main machine-description families (.md files) encode ARM, Thumb-1, Thumb-2, VFP, NEON/AdvSIMD, MVE, crypto, atomics, fixed-point, vector, and legacy iWMMXt patterns, predicates, constraints, iterators, unspecs, and instruction-type taxonomies used for lowering and scheduling. The module also contains extensive CPU/architecture databases, generated option/tuning tables, per-core pipeline models and cost tables for scheduling and performance tuning, shared Arm/AArch64 support for branch-protection and common RTL analysis, frontend integration for C and D target macros and overloaded builtins, implementation of Arm ACLE/NEON/MVE/CDE/VFP builtin and public intrinsic-header support, driver logic for native CPU detection, and OS/ABI configuration headers for ELF, Linux, BSD, RTEMS, VxWorks, semihosting, and other Arm environments. Together these file groups make this module the complete target-specific code-generation, intrinsic, tuning, and platform-configuration subsystem for 32-bit Arm in GCC.
